data.title: A notice beside the hall door
data.goal: Respond to a broad claim and write a correction with an accurate scope.

data.situation: A little later, Sam arrived with biscuits and saw the papers beside the mug. “Repairs always stop every activity,” he said. Jo pulled out a chair for him. His assertion went far beyond the Monday morning closure on the confirmed notice. She explained her earlier scepticism about the unsigned message and placed the afternoon booking record where all three could see it. Jo countered the assertion with the confirmed bookings. “The afternoon groups are still coming. The caretaker has checked that.” Sam looked from the record to the notice. Calling every activity cancelled was an exaggeration, he admitted. He drew a line through “all week” on one printed copy, but stopped before throwing it away. They needed to explain what had changed, not pretend there had been no closure. Sam began to talk about how much the biscuits had cost. Lin smiled and moved the tin away from the papers. The price was irrelevant to whether the hall would open. She brought their attention back to the times. “We must not omit the Monday morning closure from the new notice,” she said. Someone arriving at ten would still find a locked door, even though the afternoon groups could meet. At the window, they wrote a short statement: “On Monday, the hall and kitchen are closed from nine until twelve for repairs. Afternoon activities will go ahead as usual.” Sam checked the times against the caretaker’s notice. Jo pinned the new sheet beside the hall door and sent the same wording to the groups. As they left, Lin took a biscuit. The new sheet told people when they could come.
data.easySummary: Sam says repairs stop every activity. Jo counters his assertion with afternoon bookings. They remove the exaggeration, keep the real Monday morning closure, and put an accurate statement beside the hall door.
data.easySummaryZh: 萨姆说维修让所有活动停下来。乔用下午预约反驳他的断言。她们去掉夸大说法，保留确实存在的周一早上关闭，再把准确说明贴到大厅门旁。

retrievalPrompts.cue: Sam says repairs always stop every activity. You have checked afternoon bookings. Explain why you doubt his claim and answer it with the record.
retrievalPrompts.cueZh: 萨姆说维修总会让所有活动停下来，你已核对下午预约。说明为什么怀疑这个说法，并用记录回应。
acceptableAnswers: I have some scepticism about the assertion. I can counter it with the confirmed afternoon bookings.

retrievalPrompts.cue: All activities were said to be cancelled, but afternoon groups will meet. Explain what is wrong with the wording.
retrievalPrompts.cueZh: 有人说所有活动都取消，但下午的小组仍会聚会。说明原措辞有什么问题。
acceptableAnswers: Saying that every activity has been cancelled is an exaggeration. The closure is only on Monday morning.

retrievalPrompts.function: Between the tin and the notice
retrievalPrompts.cue: The discussion turns to biscuit prices. Bring it back to opening times and explain what the new notice must include.
retrievalPrompts.cueZh: 讨论转到饼干价格。把它拉回开放时间，并说明新通知必须包含什么。
acceptableAnswers: The biscuit price is irrelevant to whether the hall opens. We must not omit the Monday morning closure from our statement.

transferPrompt.cue: A friend says platform repairs have stopped every train. A confirmed timetable shows only two early trains cancelled. Give a correction that keeps those cancellations and answers the larger claim.
transferPrompt.cueZh: 朋友说站台维修让所有列车停运。已确认的时刻表显示仅两班早间列车取消。写一段更正，保留这两班取消的事实并回应更大的说法。
acceptableAnswers: That assertion is an exaggeration. The timetable counters it: only two early trains are cancelled. The statement must not omit those cancellations.
